guidance.summary: Newmont reiterated its 2026 production (5.3 million attributable gold ounces) and capital guidance ($1.95 billion sustaining, $1.4 billion development), improved 2026 CAS and AISC guidance to $925 and $1,520 per ounce, and indicated 2027 production growth of a low-to-mid single-digit percentage with higher unit costs and roughly $500 million more development capital.

guidance.sentence: On track to meet Newmont's full-year 2026 production guidance 2 of 5.3 million attributable gold ounces; produced 1.3 million attributable gold ounces, as well as 11 million ounces of silver and 23 thousand tonnes of copper, primarily from Newmont's managed operations

Gold by-product Costs Applicable to Sales (CAS) was $832 per ounce and All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) was $1,454 per ounce 3 ; improved full-year cost guidance to $925 and $1,520 per ounce, respectively 2

Newmont expects to spend $1.95 billion in 2026 in sustaining capital through targeted investments in critical infrastructure, including tailings solutions, as detailed in the '2026 Guidance Expectations' section below.

Newmont expects to invest $1.4 billion of development capital in 2026 as it advances the highest-return free cash flow generative projects, while continuing to study, evaluate and define the future growth profile of its portfolio.
Newmont expects total attributable gold production in the fourth quarter of 2026 to be the strongest quarter of the year, driven by several of its managed operations.

Although Newmont's full-year cost guidance has improved, unit costs are expected to increase in the fourth quarter primarily due to higher sustaining capital spend, as well as lower co-product volumes.

Newmont has provided an enhanced oil price sensitivity for the indirect exposure through key consumables and inputs, which is expected to result in an additional approximate $50 million cost impact for every $10 change in price per barrel of oil.
Sustaining and development capital spend are expected to be the highest of the year in the fourth quarter, with full-year 2026 guidance remaining unchanged.

The balances as of the end of the third quarter are before the planned payment of $1.95 billion to Barrick under the terms of the amended NGM agreement, which is expected to be paid in the fourth quarter of 2026.
Newmont expects to return to production growth in 2027, with attributable gold production expected to increase by a low-to-mid single-digit percentage compared to 2026.

Newmont expects unit costs to trend higher in 2027 reflecting inflation escalation above the 3 percent assumption incorporated for 2026 guidance, as well as higher diesel prices, unfavorable foreign exchange movements, particularly related to the Australian dollar, and continued royalty sensitivities driven by the gold price.
Sustaining capital spend in 2027 is anticipated to be largely in line with 2026 levels, as Newmont continues to progress the tailings work at Cadia and Boddington.

Development capital spend is expected to increase by approximately $500 million compared to 2026 as investment ramps up on the construction of the Lihir Nearshore Barrier and the Red Chris Block Cave project, pending a full-funds investment decision.
Newmont anticipates 2026 spending of approximately $850 million for the total portfolio and approximately $550 million on the Yanacocha water treatment plants.
Total reclamation spend is expected to decrease sequentially by approximately $200 million per year through 2028.

writeup.headline: Newmont rates Buy on very strong margins, a net-cash balance sheet and absolutely low cash-flow multiples.
writeup.thesis: Newmont scores 76, a Buy, carried mainly by quality (97) and balance sheet (98): an operating margin of 51.8%, an FCF margin of 37.9%, diluted share count down 4.5% year on year, and net cash with cash at 1.74 times debt. Valuation scores 83 because the multiples are low in absolute terms, with P/FCF of 11.8x, EV/EBIT of 8.3x and an FCF yield 3.5 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock sits near the middle: P/FCF is cheaper than at 59 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/S is more expensive than at 48 of the last 61 month-ends. Growth (66) is solid, with TTM revenue growth of 23.7% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 15.2% year on year. Trend and news (both 56) hold the score back: the price is 6.1% below its 50-day average and 15.7% below its 52-week high, and the Q3 guidance improved 2026 costs but flagged higher 2027 costs.
key_risks: Results depend heavily on the gold price, and October spot gold sat below the price assumed in Newmont's guidance.
2027 guidance points to higher unit costs and about $500 million more development capital.
Operating issues at individual mines, including lower Lihir output, drought risk there, and Cadia's earlier seismic event.
Weak recent momentum: shares are 2.8 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and 15.7% below their 52-week high.
Several analysts trimmed targets and one downgraded to Hold.
what_would_change: A 4-point score gain would reach Strong Buy, for example through a recovery in the trend factor (56) or more positive news and guidance.
A 12-point drop would cut the rating to Hold, which could come from a falling gold price hurting margins, growth and valuation together.
Further negative guidance on 2027 costs or capital, or more analyst downgrades, would pull the news score down.
Any slowing of revenue growth from the current TTM revenue growth of 23.7% would weigh on the growth factor.
